blocks.title: You'll want to know: びょういん

segments.text: びょういん — byōin — "a hospital".

Four beats: byo–o–i–n. The first sign is ひ with the voicing mark, so hi becomes bi, and a small ょ joins it into one beat, byo. The rest, う, い and ん, you already write. The next lesson writes the first sign.
Keep the ょ small. With a full-size よ the word would be biyōin, a hair salon.

segments.text: ひ hi + ゛ becomes び bi.
Write ひ in full, in the order you learned it. Then add the two short strokes of the voicing mark at the upper right, beside the high right end, the left one first.
The h row voices to b here too. With び (bi), you write all five: ば, び (bi), ぶ, べ and ぼ.
With a small ょ and ういん after it, you can now write the word from the last lesson: びょういん, byōin, a hospital.
Write ひ, then び, and say hi, bi.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: どようび

segments.text: どようび — doyōbi — "Saturday".

The new sign is spent at once. ど, よ and う, then び: four beats, do–yo–o–bi. The う stretches the o, as it does in きのう. The last part, yōbi, means a day of the week, and the name of every day ends in it. You write every sign in it now.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: いりぐち

segments.text: いりぐち — iriguchi — "an entrance, the way in". You see it on signs at stations and shops.
Four beats: i–ri–gu–chi. い, り and ち you already write. The third sign is く with the voicing mark, so ku becomes gu. The next lesson writes it.
The guchi is kuchi, "a mouth", voiced where it joins the word in front of it: an entrance is the mouth you go in by.

segments.text: く ku + ゛ becomes ぐ gu.
Write く in full: one stroke, down to the left and back down to the right. Then add the two short strokes of the voicing mark at the upper right, beside the point, the left one first.
The k row voices to g, as か did to が in ありがとう and こ to ご in ございます.
With いり in front and ち after it, you can now write the word from the last lesson: いりぐち, iriguchi, an entrance.
Write く, then ぐ, and say ku, gu.
Write か が, こ ご and く ぐ (gu) in pairs, and say each one.
Write いりぐち from memory and say iriguchi.
Stop after one accurate form.
Source: Unicode Hiragana chart.

blocks.title: You'll want to know: でぐち

segments.text: でぐち — deguchi — "an exit, the way out".

The new sign is spent at once, beside one from the last chapter: で, then ぐ and ち, three beats, de–gu–chi. The guchi is the same voiced "mouth" as in いりぐち (iriguchi). On a sign, the two words face each other: the way in, and the way out. You write every sign in both now.

segments.text: き ki + ゛ becomes ぎ gi.

Write き in full: the two bars, the long diagonal with its hook, then the separate curve. Then add the two short strokes of the voicing mark at the upper right, beside the ends of the bars, the left one first.
That completes the g row: が, ぎ (gi), ぐ (gu), げ (ge), ご.
With んこう after it, you can now write the word from the last lesson: ぎんこう, ginkō, a bank.
Write き, then ぎ, and say ki, gi.
Write が ぎ (gi) ぐ (gu) げ (ge) ご in a row, and say it.
